newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums steady, U.S. cargo offered.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums steady, U.S. cargo offered.

text.p: A big winter freeze across northern Europe maintained a solid floor under NWE gas oil cargo premiums on Wednesday but volumes sold were meagre, traders said.
Iced-up canals continue to curb barge buying interest and encourage truck and train transport, while French buying interest for cargoes almost disappeared, the traders said.
German winter grade heating oil was unchanged at around Feb IPE +$7.50/9 cif NWE. French quality was around Feb IPE +$7/8 cif Le Havre for January 10-20.

Heating oil buying interest into Bordeaux was bid at around Feb +$8.75. Traders reported buying interest into La Pallice for low sulphur diesel but no numbers emerged. A U.S. cargo of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was offered at about Feb +6.
Benchmark Jan IPE futures was unchanged at $229.50 a tonne at 1219 GMT and Feb IPE was down $1 a tonne at $225.25, pressured by news of growing U.S. distillate stocks.
Barge trade was quiet. Prompt refinery grade heating oil barges were unchanged at around Jan IPE +$2.25/3.25 basis Rotterdam with January 20-30 around Jan IPE +$1.50/2.50.
Low sulphur diesel barges were offered at Jan +$10 from Amsterdam and at Jan IPE +$13 from Flushing.
